result:
Fixed `scenario.json` in place.

What changed: compressed the engineered relative clause into three plain adjectives — the request now reads "…assigned to the active human admin." Condition c4's text was updated to match; its fact list and all decoys, seed, query, and write are unchanged ("active" → A:User.active, "human" → A:User.app, "admin" → A:User.admin).

What I kept and why: attribute-based reference with no name or issue key. Naming the assignee would make every decoy fail the name condition in addition to its flag, so a solver could pass every probe without ever checking active/admin/app — the exact thing this scenario must test. Attribute-only identification is also the genre (the worked examples identify the file/event by attributes, not ids). Each adjective now does visible work against a real alternative in the seed — a deactivated ex-admin, a non-admin member, and an admin bot account — so a careful reader can see why the speaker bothered.
